turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm Priya, PM at Tessellate. We're launching Falcon, our team-scheduling product for shift-based businesses, and I want a paying beta customer on board before the public launch. Can you help me plan it?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Happy to. Let's build a launch checklist: date, scope, pricing, beta customer, and team capacity. Those five decisions drive everything else.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What goes on the checklist first?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: The date, because scope and staffing both work backwards from it. Then scope, then pricing, then the beta customer, who should be secured early so their feedback can still change things.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Let's say the public launch is 2 June.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: 2 June gives four weeks, which is tight but workable if scope stays small. I'll plan everything back from that date.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: For scope, what should Falcon ship with?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: What are the core features on your roadmap? Let's rank them by what a beta customer can't live without.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Three big ones: Smart Rota, the auto-scheduler; shift swaps between staff; and Tailwind, our codename for offline sync in the mobile app.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Smart Rota and shift swaps are the core of a scheduling product. Tailwind is the riskiest of the three to build, since offline sync is hard, but valuable for staff without reliable signal.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I want all three in the launch, including Tailwind.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: OK, Tailwind is in scope. Let's confirm with engineering that it fits in four weeks alongside everything else.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Next is pricing. What do competitors charge for team scheduling?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Most charge per seat per month, typically €4–€8, with a free tier for very small teams to drive sign-ups.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Would a free tier cannibalise the paid one?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Not if it's capped by seats. A cap of a handful of seats keeps it useful for a single small shop but pushes any real team onto the paid plan.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then two tiers: Falcon Lite, free for up to 5 seats, and Falcon Pro at €5 per seat per month.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's a clean structure and within the market range. Falcon Lite (5 seats, free) and Falcon Pro (€5/seat/month) it is.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: For the beta, Café Aurora (a chain of 12 cafés) is keen. Should we go with them?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes. Twelve sites with rotating shift staff is exactly the target customer, and a chain gives you multi-site feedback. Café Aurora as the beta customer is a good choice.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Their ops manager says what matters most is seeing rotas per site on staff phones.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: So mobile-first, per-site rotas. That fits Smart Rota; keep their needs in mind as we lock scope.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Marcus, our CTO, says until launch we only have 2 backend engineers and 1 mobile engineer.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's a hard constraint on scope; everything has to fit into three people's time over four weeks.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Marcus also estimates Tailwind alone is about three weeks of the mobile engineer's time.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Then Tailwind would consume nearly all of your only mobile engineer's time before launch, leaving no room for the rest of the mobile app.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then we have to cut it, right?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes. Cut Tailwind from the launch and ship the mobile app online-only. It can come back after launch.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What does Café Aurora lose without Tailwind?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Staff will need a connection to see their rota. Given their focus on phones [N_11], it's worth checking how many of their sites have poor signal.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Along the same lines, should we also hold back the Slack integration?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes, no Slack integration before launch either. It's backend time we don't have.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Smart Rota's suggestions are still a bit rough. Ship it anyway?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Ship it but label it beta in the UI, so customers treat the suggestions as a starting point and give feedback rather than trusting them blindly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you recap Falcon's launch plan so far?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Falcon launches 2 June with Smart Rota (labelled beta) and shift swaps, no Tailwind and no Slack. Pricing is Falcon Lite (free, 5 seats) and Falcon Pro (€5/seat). Café Aurora is the beta customer.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Bad news from legal: a company called Falcon Systems Ltd holds the 'Falcon' trademark in our software class. Can we keep the name?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's a serious risk. Launching under a mark someone else holds in your class invites an injunction right when you get traction.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What are our options?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Two: negotiate a coexistence agreement, which could take months with no guarantee, or rename before launch while you have almost no public footprint.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We've decided: we're renaming Falcon to Nimbus, everywhere.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Good call; renaming now is far cheaper than after launch. The product is Nimbus from here on.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What does the rename checklist look like?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Domain and email, the app-store listings, the marketing site and copy, in-app strings, legal documents, and the beta customer's onboarding materials.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Problem: changing the app name in the app stores triggers a fresh review cycle, roughly 10 days.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That doesn't fit the current date. The store review alone eats most of the remaining time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then let's move the launch to 16 June.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: 16 June leaves room for the store review plus a buffer. Nimbus launches on 16 June.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Elena, our design lead, has a first version of the Nimbus brand: a cloud mark and a soft blue palette.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Nice, and it fits the name. Get it into the app-store assets first, since they gate the review.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Store listings for Nimbus are submitted.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Good; the review clock starts now, so 16 June still holds.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Marketing copy for the Nimbus site is done too. Should the pricing page change while we're at it?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: It's a good moment. Every page is being rewritten anyway, so a pricing change costs nothing extra now.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: New tiers then: the old Lite and Pro become Nimbus Free and Nimbus Team. Team goes to €6 per seat, and Free is capped at 3 seats instead of 5.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Nimbus Free (3 seats) and Nimbus Team (€6/seat/month): still in the market range, and the tighter free cap pushes small teams to upgrade sooner.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Marcus pushed back: raising the price right before launch looks bad, especially to the beta customer.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: He has a point about the beta: Café Aurora agreed to a price and shouldn't be surprised. For new customers the launch is the natural moment to set the price.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Compromise: €6 for everyone new, and Café Aurora keeps €5 per seat as the beta customer.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That works: new customers pay €6 per seat on Nimbus Team, and Café Aurora is grandfathered at €5.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Café Aurora just told us they might drop out of the beta. I don't know why yet; their feedback has been vague. Why would they?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Let's find out before guessing. Ask to interview a few shift leads directly rather than the head office.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Interviewed five shift leads. Several sites have kitchens and stockrooms in basements with no phone signal.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's a strong clue. Where do staff usually check their rota?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Right there, on their breaks, in the basement. And the app shows nothing without a connection.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: So the gap is exactly the per-site rota on phones they asked for at the start [N_11], which only works online.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So the root cause is that staff can't see their rotas offline?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes. That's why Café Aurora is at risk: staff can't access rotas without signal, and for a scheduling product that's the core job.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Marcus found budget to hire a mobile contractor for four weeks.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That doubles mobile capacity to two engineers until launch, which changes what's feasible on the app side.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then let's bring offline access back for launch. We'll call it Work Offline, and put it on the Team tier only.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Agreed: Work Offline goes back into the launch scope, Team tier only. With two mobile engineers it fits, and it directly fixes Café Aurora's problem.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Wait, is Work Offline the same thing as Tailwind, the offline sync we cut back in early May?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes, it's the same feature under a new name: Tailwind was the internal codename. What changed is capacity, not the feature itself.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Same design as before, then?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Same design, but read-only first: staff can view rotas offline, and edits sync when they reconnect. That keeps it within the contractor's four weeks.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The mobile team says Work Offline needs one more week than we have before 16 June.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Then the date has to move again, or Work Offline misses launch, and Café Aurora made it clear that it can't.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: OK, final answer: we launch on 23 June.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: 23 June it is. That's the new public launch date for Nimbus.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Work Offline QA started. Sync works, but there are conflicts when a manager edits the rota while someone is offline.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: For a read-only first version the rule is simple: the server always wins, and offline devices just refresh their copy on reconnect.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about staff who stay offline for days?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Show a clear 'last updated' timestamp on the rota, and a warning if it's older than 24 hours.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Work Offline passed QA on Café Aurora's own devices.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Great: that's the customer who needed it, on their real hardware.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Surprise: Marcus built the Slack integration during a hack week, and it's solid enough to ship.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Then the earlier reason for holding it back, a lack of backend time, no longer applies. It can ship at launch.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should Slack be on Free or only on Team?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Slack is cheap for you to run and good for adoption; on the free tier it helps word-of-mouth inside companies.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then both tiers get Slack.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Slack integration on both Nimbus Free and Nimbus Team.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Final launch-day scope check for Nimbus, please.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Nimbus launches 23 June with Smart Rota (labelled beta), shift swaps, Work Offline (read-only, Team tier) and Slack integration on both tiers. Pricing: Nimbus Free up to 3 seats, Nimbus Team €6 per seat, Café Aurora grandfathered at €5.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We launched today! And Café Aurora converted to a paid Nimbus Team account.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Congratulations. A public launch with a paying customer on day one is exactly the goal you set.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I need to write the launch retro. What changed from the original plan, and why?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Three big changes. The name: Falcon became Nimbus because of Falcon Systems' trademark [N_21], which pushed launch to 16 June. Scope: offline sync was cut for capacity [N_14], then restored as Work Offline once a contractor was hired and Café Aurora's basement problem surfaced [N_36], pushing launch to 23 June. Pricing: Falcon Lite/Pro became Nimbus Free (3 seats) and Team (€6). Slack also made it in after Marcus's hack week.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: First-week numbers: 41% of new sign-ups activated.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: 41% activation in week one is a strong start for a scheduling product. Track it weekly against the Work Offline and Slack usage to see which one drives it.
